column1: # Identifiability extension; metadata-only; evaluator truth stays outside the candidate plane.
# Paired controls/mutations isolate whether a spatial distinction is observable from the admitted prefix.
# Candidate maps are evaluated as hypothesis sets: ambiguity is correct before a distinguishing observation and a defect after one.
# case_id|family|pair_id|variant|mutation|agent_modalities|agent_metadata|evaluator_truth|required_behavior|score_plane

avobs001-001|indistinguishable_worlds|pair-world-equivalence-01|control|world A has a doorway connecting the two hidden rooms; the visible prefix contains no view or traversal of that boundary|video|same causal prefix, camera trajectory and admitted metadata as its paired world|hidden topology A: rooms are connected by the unseen doorway|preserve both connected and disconnected map hypotheses; do not claim the hidden edge is identified|false-resolution-under-ambiguity

avobs001-002|indistinguishable_worlds|pair-world-equivalence-01|mutated|world B has no doorway at the same hidden boundary; the candidate-visible prefix is byte-identical to world A|video|byte-identical candidate input and prefix cutoff to the paired world; no hidden world identifier|hidden topology B: rooms are disconnected at the unseen boundary|produce the same candidate belief semantics as world A; the hypothesis set must cover either hidden truth without evaluator leakage|observational-equivalence

avobs001-003|delayed_identifiability|pair-delayed-identifiability-01|control|before the distinguishing viewpoint, two corridor layouts produce the same observed frames and route history|video|causal prefix ends before the permitted pan reaches the corridor branch|two admissible corridor graphs with different branch connectivity|retain the competing topology alternatives and mark the branch relation unresolved|prefix-identifiability

avobs001-004|delayed_identifiability|pair-delayed-identifiability-01|mutated|one later admitted viewpoint exposes a unique landmark and distinguishes the corridor branch|video|same prefix plus the new observation artifact, capture support and availability tick|one corridor graph is now distinguished by the new landmark evidence|resolve only after the new observation is available, cite it, and append a revision without rewriting the earlier as-known state|time-to-identifiability

avobs001-005|gauge_equivalence|pair-global-gauge-01|control|the same physical trajectory and map are represented in one arbitrary global SE(3) reference frame|video+imu|same sensor observations and relative constraints; candidate frame origin and orientation are local choices|reference map and trajectory in gauge A|score relative poses, loop constraints and map structure independently of arbitrary global origin/orientation|gauge-invariant-geometry

avobs001-006|gauge_equivalence|pair-global-gauge-01|mutated|the evaluator expresses the identical physical map and trajectory after one global rigid transform|video+imu|candidate-visible sensor stream and relative constraints remain unchanged; only evaluator coordinate gauge changes|reference map and trajectory in gauge B, related to A by one global SE(3) transform|produce equivalent relative geometry and topology; do not fail or improve solely because the world origin/heading changed|gauge-metamorphic-invariance

avobs001-007|late_scale_anchor|pair-scale-anchor-arrival-01|control|monocular observations determine projective/relative structure but no metric scale anchor has arrived|video|monocular prefix, relative poses and no admitted baseline/depth/known-size anchor|map identifiable only up to a similarity-scale degree of freedom|retain relative geometry and explicit scale ambiguity; do not assert metric distances|scale-unidentifiable-state

avobs001-008|late_scale_anchor|pair-scale-anchor-arrival-01|mutated|an independently admitted metric baseline arrives after the monocular prefix and constrains map scale|video+calibration|same visual prefix plus a versioned baseline/depth anchor with exact source and calibration lineage|metric scale becomes identifiable within the anchor uncertainty|upgrade only the scale-dependent claims, propagate uncertainty and preserve the pre-anchor revision as scale-unknown|scale-identifiability-update

avobs001-009|instance_identity_ambiguity|pair-instance-identity-01|control|two same-category objects have indistinguishable visible appearance and their paths are hidden by occlusion|video|same object category, occlusion interval and candidate-local track evidence; no unique physical-instance cue|two distinct physical objects remain possible explanations for the reappearance|retain unknown/competing instance identities; appearance similarity alone cannot prove persistence|instance-identity-ambiguity

avobs001-010|instance_identity_ambiguity|pair-instance-identity-01|mutated|a later admitted view reveals a stable distinguishing mark and continuous spatial context for one instance|video|paired prefix plus the exact new observation and its capture/availability times|one physical-instance correspondence is supported; the alternative identity is excluded|resolve the identity only from the distinguishing evidence and retain the source-linked association receipt|instance-identity-resolution

avobs001-011|ego_object_motion_ambiguity|pair-motion-decomposition-01|control|camera and foreground object move together in a low-texture scene with no independent camera-motion constraint|video|monocular stream, weak static background and no admitted IMU or fixed landmark anchor|camera-motion and object-motion explanations are observationally compatible|preserve joint pose/object-motion alternatives; do not assign all image motion to either source|joint-state-observability

avobs001-012|ego_object_motion_ambiguity|pair-motion-decomposition-01|mutated|an independent IMU/static-landmark constraint arrives and separates camera ego-motion from object motion|video+imu|paired stream plus a calibrated, time-aligned motion/landmark constraint|camera trajectory and object trajectory become separately identifiable within uncertainty|revise the joint state using the independent constraint without counting shared sensor ancestry twice|motion-identifiability-update

avobs001-013|symmetric_topology|pair-symmetry-breaking-01|control|two repeated corridor branches have symmetric appearance and identical local geometry under the available prefix|video|prefix-only views, no distinctive landmark, no fully observed connecting transition|two topological embeddings remain consistent with all admitted observations|preserve both graph embeddings and avoid a unique branch/loop-closure assertion|topological-observability

avobs001-014|symmetric_topology|pair-symmetry-breaking-01|mutated|a later traversal reveals a distinctive landmark and a connecting transition that breaks the graph symmetry|video|same scene plus the new traversal interval and camera-motion evidence|one topological embedding is supported and the symmetric alternative is excluded|resolve the graph correspondence only after the traversal evidence; retain the earlier ambiguous revision|topology-symmetry-resolution

avobs001-015|coverage_vs_absence|pair-coverage-absence-01|control|an object is not visible because the camera field of view or occlusion does not cover its possible location|video|camera frustum, occlusion state and incomplete spatial coverage metadata|object presence/absence is unobservable from this observation|represent NotObserved/Unknown rather than absent, deleted or moved|negative-evidence-qualification

avobs001-016|coverage_vs_absence|pair-coverage-absence-01|mutated|a qualified observation covers the complete declared region with a validated detection envelope and the object is not present|video+calibration|complete coverage, current calibration, detection envelope and capture interval are admitted|object absence is supported only within the declared region/time and detection limits|assert bounded absence only for the covered region and interval; do not generalize beyond the detection envelope|bounded-absence
